top_story_title: Check Point Security Gateways exploited in the wild: PHP2Shell plus a Gaia OS root escalation, ending in a backdoor and wiped ESXi files
top_story_summary: Check Point has released emergency hotfixes for a high-severity flaw that attackers have been exploiting since late October to gain root privileges and persist on Security Gateways. Check Point's own research describes activity that began on 30 October 2026: an unknown threat actor used the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities for initial access on unpatched gateways, then chained a previously unreported local privilege escalation in Gaia OS - tracked as CVE-2026-123039 - to reach root and deploy a backdoor called TSGA. Initial targeting was against Israeli organisations, with a broader follow-up reported.
top_actions: Inventory every Check Point Security Gateway and its running Gaia OS version; prioritise any gateway with an internet-facing portal or administrative service.
Apply the emergency hotfix - check the Check Point advisory for the fixed release for your Gaia OS train, as the published reporting does not state a build number.

Treat any gateway that was exposed and unpatched before 30 October 2026 as potentially compromised: rotate local admin credentials, API keys, certificates and VPN pre-shared keys after patching, because a pre-patch compromise survives the upgrade.
Remove management access (HTTPS/SSH/API) from untrusted and internet-facing interfaces; restrict it to a dedicated management VLAN or out-of-band network.
Export and diff the gateway configuration against a known-good copy: unexpected admin users, scripts, static routes or modified login pages.
executive_summary: Check Point Security Gateways are under active exploitation: PHP2Shell for initial access, then CVE-2026-123039 in Gaia OS for root, ending in the TSGA backdoor and wiped ESXi files. Emergency hotfixes are out - patch and assume pre-patch compromise.

Cisco's October 2026 Node.js advisory carries CVE-2026-111497, a Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write that is on the CISA KEV list (added 2026-10-27, remediation due 2026-11-10 - that date has passed). Three further TLS and DNS validation flaws are in the same advisory.

Citrix patched a batch of NetScaler ADC, NetScaler Gateway and NetScaler Console flaws including CVE-2026-120868 (CVSS 9.3) and an authentication bypass. No exploitation reported yet, but NetScaler has a history of being hit fast after disclosure.

Cisco issued an informational advisory on the emergency distrust of eMudhra root and intermediate CAs: private keys for eight intermediates are brute-forceable in seconds because of a broken April 2025 key generation ceremony. Check which of your devices trust that chain.
No genuinely AI-related network-device item in this window; the AI section carries forward.
key_actions: **Check Point** — Apply the Check Point emergency hotfix for your Gaia OS version; confirm the fixed release from the vendor advisory rather than from news coverage.
**Check Point** — Patch HA pairs secondary first inside the change window, then fail over and patch the primary.

**Cisco** — Read the Cisco advisory's affected-product table and map it to your inventory by product and running version; do not assume a product is unaffected until it appears in the not-affected list.
**Cisco** — Apply the Cisco software updates that address these CVEs; the advisory states no workaround is offered via this route, so schedule the upgrade.
**Citrix** — Identify every NetScaler ADC, Gateway and Console instance and its exact firmware branch; include units that only serve internal traffic.
**Citrix** — Apply the Citrix fixed builds to all units in the device group and verify configuration sync afterwards; patch the Console before the managed appliances.
**Check Point** — Deploy the emergency hotfix on every affected gateway now rather than at the next scheduled maintenance window; take the fixed release from the vendor advisory.
**Check Point** — After patching, rotate local admin credentials, API keys, certificates and VPN pre-shared keys on any device that was exposed while unpatched.

headlines.title: Hackers Exploit PHP2Shell Flaws in Check Point Gateways to Deploy TSGA Backdoor and Wipe ESXi Files
headlines.summary: Attackers chained the PHP2Shell flaws with a Gaia OS privilege escalation to get root on unpatched Check Point Security Gateways, deploy the TSGA backdoor and wipe ESXi files.

headlines.title: Vulnerabilities in Node.js and Brotli Affecting Cisco Products: October 2026
headlines.summary: Cisco's October 2026 advisory covers four Node.js flaws affecting Cisco products, including a KEV-listed Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write that can reach remote code execution.

headlines.title: Citrix Patches 12 NetScaler and Secure Access Client Flaws, Including Authentication Bypass
headlines.summary: Citrix patched 12 flaws across NetScaler ADC, NetScaler Gateway, NetScaler Console and Secure Access Client, including an authentication bypass and CVE-2026-120868 at CVSS 9.3.

headlines.title: Check Point warns of zero-day flaw exploited for root access
headlines.summary: Check Point shipped emergency hotfixes for a high-severity flaw that attackers have exploited since late October to gain root and persist on its gateways.

headlines.title: Cisco Informational for Emergency Distrust of eMudhra Root and Intermediate Certificate Authorities
headlines.summary: Cisco issued an informational advisory on the emergency distrust of eMudhra CAs, whose eight intermediate private keys can be brute-forced in seconds after a broken 2025 key ceremony.

headlines.title: PHP2Shell Exploited in Destructive Check Point Gateway Attacks
headlines.summary: SecurityWeek identifies CVE-2026-123039 as the privilege escalation that took attackers to root on Check Point gateways after PHP2Shell gave them initial access.
